editorial:
Imagine meeting a guy who seems totally normal, like the guy who comes to fix your office printer, but has a dark secret. You get to follow Warren Stacy, a man who snaps and kills women when they turn him down. He is scary because he is smart; he kills while naked so he doesn't leave any fabric or hair behind, and he always has a perfect excuse for where he was. You will spend most of the movie watching a game of cat and mouse between him and Leo Kessler, a grumpy old detective who knows Stacy is the killer but just cannot prove it. The vibe is tense and gritty, making you feel the frustration of the police as the killer slips through their fingers time and again.

What really works here is the acting and the way the tension builds up. You will love watching the detective push the rules and do things he probably shouldn't just to get a win. While the pacing slows down a bit in the middle, the ending makes up for it. If you love old-school crime thrillers, you should definitely check this one out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night, or if you really love physical media, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your collection is a great way to see those 80s visuals in high quality.
endingExplained: The movie ends with a final showdown where the detective finally traps Stacy. After a long game of tricks, the detective manages to break through Stacy's perfect alibis. In the final scenes, the killer's arrogance becomes his downfall. He is caught in a way that leaves him with no more excuses. The police finally get the evidence they need, and the cycle of murders ends with Stacy being arrested and taken away.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic police procedurals and psychological cat-and-mouse games.
